name: DeepSeek-R1 incentivizes reasoning in LLMs through reinforcement learning
authors: DeepSeek-AI (corresponding: research@deepseek.com); Daya Guo, Dejian Yang, Haowei Zhang, Junxiao Song, Ruoyu Zhang, Runxin Xu, Qihao Zhu, Shirong Ma, Peiyi Wang, Xiao Bi, et al. (very large author list, ~200 authors). Lead affiliation: DeepSeek-AI (Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., affiliated with High-Flyer), China.
venue: Nature 2025 (vol. 645, pp. 633-638; published online 17 Sep 2025; DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-09422-z). Originally arXiv preprint 2501.12948 (22 Jan 2025). Semantic Scholar CorpusID:275789950; PubMed 40962978; PMC12443585.
code_url: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1 (trained weights of DeepSeek-R1-Zero, DeepSeek-R1 and six distilled dense models released under MIT license; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15753193; inference script at https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15753347; models also on HuggingFace).
reflection_type: RL-emergent verbal-self-critique within a single long chain-of-thought, plus an outcome/tool-verified training signal. There is NO learned critic model, NO multi-agent debate, and NO external search/MCTS at inference. The reflective behaviour (revisiting/reevaluating prior steps, self-verification, exploring alternative approaches, the 'aha moment') emerges spontaneously inside the model's own CoT as a by-product of GRPO RL against verifiable rewards. The improvement SIGNAL is verifiable reward (rule-based accuracy + format), i.e. tool/oracle-verified outcomes, distilled into weights; the reflective COMPETENCE is emergent in-context self-critique. Best summarized as: RL-emergent in-CoT self-reflection/verification trained via verifiable-reward RL.
feedback_source: environment-reward / verifiable-reward, specifically a rule-based reward system: (1) accuracy rewards from ground-truth answer checking (deterministic math answers boxed and string/rule-matched; code competition answers verified by a compiler against predefined test cases) and (2) format rewards enforcing <think>...</think> tags. For DeepSeek-R1's later stages a generative/model-based reward (DeepSeek-V3 as judge for non-rule-checkable data) and trained helpfulness/safety reward models are added. The authors deliberately AVOID outcome/process neural reward models during R1-Zero RL because they invite reward hacking. No human-annotated CoT, no unit-test scaffold beyond the compiler check, no hidden-state probe.
iteration_structure: For learning: an online RL loop (GRPO) with grouped rollouts per question (16 samples/question, batch 512, reference model refreshed every 400 steps). DeepSeek-R1 adds a multi-stage outer loop: cold-start SFT -> reasoning-oriented RL -> rejection-sampling SFT (~800k samples) -> preference/alignment RL. At INFERENCE the model is single-pass (one long CoT) but performs iterative-refine-like behaviour WITHIN that single chain (it revisits and reevaluates steps); optional majority-voting/self-consistency (cons@64 / cons@16) is reported as an add-on. It is NOT episodic-retry-with-reset, NOT tree/MCTS search (MCTS was tried and abandoned), NOT population/evolutionary.
reflection_object: Primarily model weights (the policy is updated by RL so that it natively produces self-reflective reasoning chains). The unit being reflected on/modified at inference is the reasoning chain (CoT): the model revisits and reevaluates its own intermediate reasoning steps, verifies partial results, and switches strategy mid-chain. It does NOT modify prompts/context, maintain an episodic memory store, edit a skill library, or alter its own code; the reusable artifact produced (for distillation) is the set of reasoning trajectories, but the locus of change for the method itself is weights + the emergent in-CoT reasoning trace.
learning_locus: gradient_weight_update. The core contribution is realized through large-scale RL (GRPO) gradient updates on DeepSeek-V3-Base; reasoning/self-reflection capability is baked into parameters. (At inference the model then exhibits in-context verbal self-reflection, but that capability is a product of the weight update, not an in-context-only scaffold.) Distillation to smaller models is via SFT (also weight updates).
requires_training: RL (GRPO / online, group-relative policy optimization) is the central method. DeepSeek-R1-Zero = pure RL on the base model with NO SFT cold start. DeepSeek-R1 = nested-RL+SFT: cold-start SFT (thousands of long-CoT examples) -> reasoning RL (GRPO) -> rejection-sampling SFT on ~800k samples (600k reasoning + 200k non-reasoning, 2 epochs) -> a second preference/alignment RL stage (rule-based reasoning rewards + helpfulness/safety reward models). Distilled models (1.5B-70B) use SFT only (no RL).
reward_or_critic_model: verifiable reward (rule-based: accuracy + format) is the primary signal and the headline claim (pure verifiable-reward RL incentivizes reasoning). GRPO uses NO value/critic network (advantages are estimated from the group reward distribution instead of a learned baseline). The authors explicitly REJECT neural process reward models (PRM) and outcome reward models for the main RL because of reward hacking. Later R1 stages add a generative reward (DeepSeek-V3-as-judge) for non-verifiable data and trained helpfulness (pairwise, 66k pairs) and safety (pointwise, 106k prompts) reward models for alignment.
distillation_target: model-weights (twofold). (1) The RL-discovered self-reflective reasoning is distilled into the policy's own weights. (2) Explicitly, the reasoning patterns of the large DeepSeek-R1 are distilled into six smaller dense models (Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B/7B, Qwen2.5-14B/32B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct) by SFT on ~800k DeepSeek-R1-generated reasoning samples. The paper shows distillation from the large model BEATS running RL directly on the small model (e.g., on Qwen2.5-32B), establishing model-weight distillation as a key deliverable. Not episodic-memory, skill-library, prompt, or constitution.
emergent_vs_engineered: RL-emergent (this is the canonical example). DeepSeek-R1-Zero is explicitly the first open demonstration that self-reflection, verification and dynamic strategy adaptation EMERGE from pure RL against verifiable rewards, without any prompt/scaffold engineering of the reflection itself and without human CoT demonstrations. Hallmarks: spontaneously increasing 'thinking time'/response length over training; the 'aha moment' (a sudden spike in the word 'wait' and self-reevaluation in an intermediate checkpoint). Contrast with Reflexion/Self-Refine, where reflection is prompt/scaffold-engineered. (The DeepSeek-R1 production pipeline does add engineered stages -- cold-start SFT, rejection sampling, alignment RL -- but the reasoning behaviour itself is RL-emergent.)
memory_type: short-term/scratchpad. The only 'memory' is the within-response chain-of-thought (the <think>...</think> reasoning trace / extended thinking tokens), which functions as a scratchpad the model writes and re-reads/revises during a single generation. There is NO external long-term episodic memory, skill library, structured note graph, or cross-session playbook. Persistence of learned skill is at the parameter level (weights), not an external memory store.
memory_persistence: within-episode for the scratchpad/CoT (it does not carry over between separate queries). The learned reasoning ability is persisted in weights and is therefore cross-task / cross-session at the capability level (it generalizes across all reasoning problems and is available in every deployment). No retained per-episode experience buffer across inference calls.
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a for an explicit memory module (there is no external memory to curate). The closest analogue is data curation in the R1 pipeline: rejection sampling from the RL checkpoint retains only correct trajectories, filters out CoT with language mixing / overly long paragraphs / code blocks, and assembles ~800k SFT samples; a generative reward model (DeepSeek-V3) judges non-rule-checkable cases. Within a single CoT, 'curation' is the model's own emergent self-verification/re-evaluation (overwrite-by-rethinking), not a stored-memory management policy.
error_localization_granularity: Training signal is holistic/outcome-level: the reward is computed on the FINAL answer correctness (+ a format check on the whole response); there is deliberately NO step-level / process-level credit assignment (the authors abandoned process reward models / PRM). However, the EMERGENT in-CoT self-reflection operates at step-level/block-level: within its reasoning chain the model revisits, reevaluates and corrects individual prior steps. So: outcome-level reward driving emergent step-level self-correction.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: Both, at different layers. The trained capability is inter-task: RL produces a reasoner whose self-reflective skill transfers across all reasoning problems and to held-out benchmarks (and is distillable to other models). At inference, the self-correction is intra-task: within a single problem's long CoT the model refines its own reasoning before answering. It does NOT transfer episodic experience across separate task instances at test time (no cross-episode memory like Reflexion/ExpeL).
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: mid-trajectory-recovery (emergent). Within a single reasoning chain the model corrects course in-flight: it reevaluates its initial approach, allocates more thinking time, and explores alternative solution paths before committing to a final answer (the 'aha moment' is exactly this in-flight reconsideration). It is not avoidance-by-retry-next-episode (no reset/retry loop) and not post-hoc revision of an already-emitted answer.
task_domains: Primarily verifiable reasoning: math, code (competitive programming), and QA/reasoning + STEM/science (graduate-level physics/chemistry/biology). Also general-alignment (helpfulness/harmlessness) and writing/open-domain QA via the later R1 stages. Reported weaker on agentic/engineering: software engineering, function calling, multi-turn, complex role-playing, structured JSON output.
benchmarks: AIME 2024 (pass@1 and cons@64 / cons@16), MATH-500, CNMO 2024, GPQA Diamond, Codeforces (Elo rating + percentile), LiveCodeBench (2024-08 to 2025-01), SWE-bench Verified, Aider, MMLU / MMLU-Redux / MMLU-Pro, C-Eval, CMMLU, DROP, IFEval, FRAMES, SimpleQA / C-SimpleQA, AlpacaEval 2.0, Arena-Hard, HumanEval-Mul. Distilled models reported on AIME 2024, MATH-500, GPQA Diamond, Codeforces, LiveCodeBench.
headline_result: Pure RL (DeepSeek-R1-Zero, GRPO on DeepSeek-V3-Base, no SFT) raises AIME 2024 pass@1 from 15.6% to 71.0% (Nature revised value 77.9%), and to 86.7% with self-consistency/majority voting, matching/surpassing OpenAI-o1-0912. DeepSeek-R1 (full multi-stage pipeline) reaches AIME 2024 79.8% pass@1, MATH-500 97.3%, GPQA Diamond 71.5%, Codeforces 2,029 Elo (96.3rd percentile, ~expert level), comparable to OpenAI-o1-1217.
baselines: OpenAI-o1-1217 and OpenAI-o1-mini and OpenAI-o1-0912 (frontier reasoning models), DeepSeek-V3 (its own non-reasoning base via conventional post-training), Claude-3.5-Sonnet-1022, GPT-4o-0513. For distilled models: QwQ-32B-Preview and the base Qwen2.5 / Llama3 instruct models, and RL-on-small-model (Qwen2.5-32B-RL) as an internal comparison.
gains_vs_baseline: DeepSeek-R1-Zero AIME 2024: +55.4 absolute (15.6% -> 71.0% pass@1; Nature: -> 77.9%), reaching o1-0912 level from a base near random. DeepSeek-R1 vs DeepSeek-V3 (its conventionally-trained sibling, same V3-Base): AIME 2024 79.8% vs 39.2%, MATH-500 97.3% vs 90.2%, GPQA Diamond 71.5% vs 59.1%, Codeforces 2029 vs 1134 Elo, LiveCodeBench 65.9% vs 36.2% -- large RL-driven gains. vs OpenAI-o1-1217: R1 slightly surpasses on AIME 2024 (79.8 vs 79.2) and is on par on MATH-500 (97.3 vs 96.4); slightly below o1 on some knowledge benchmarks. Distillation: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B (72.6 AIME, 94.3 MATH-500, 62.1 GPQA, 57.2 LiveCodeBench) far exceeds QwQ-32B-Preview (50.0 AIME) and beats running RL directly on Qwen2.5-32B; Distill-Qwen-7B (55.5 AIME) beats GPT-4o-0513 (9.3) and QwQ-32B-Preview.
compute_cost_profile: Training: large-scale RL (described as costly; precise FLOPs/$ in Supplementary Information 2.4.4, not in the main text). RL hyperparameters (R1 first stage): lr 3e-6, KL coeff 0.001, GRPO clip eps 10, sampling temp 1, 16 rollouts/question, max length 32,768 tokens, 32 questions/step (batch 512), reference model refreshed every 400 steps; 8,192 rollouts per generation split into 16 minibatches, single inner epoch. GRPO is cheaper than PPO (no value network ~ halves the trainable model footprint). Inference: a reasoning model -> markedly higher token cost than single-pass (hundreds-to-thousands of CoT tokens, capped at 32,768), but dynamically allocated by problem difficulty (fewer tokens for easy, more for hard). Distillation amortizes inference cost into much smaller dense models. Overthinking on easy questions is noted as residual inefficiency.
known_limitations: (1) DeepSeek-R1-Zero suffers poor readability and language mixing (English/Chinese mixed in one CoT) -- the motivation for the R1 cold-start pipeline. (2) Prompt sensitivity: few-shot prompting consistently DEGRADES R1; authors recommend zero-shot, direct problem statement. (3) General capability gaps vs DeepSeek-V3 in function calling, multi-turn, complex role-playing, and JSON output. (4) Language mixing persists for non-Chinese/English queries. (5) Software-engineering tasks under-improved because long eval times limited RL there (SWE-bench Verified ~ comparable to V3, not dominant). (6) Overthinking: excessive reasoning on simple questions; token-efficiency room remains. (7) Reward hacking risk: pure RL needs reliable verifiable rewards; for non-verifiable tasks (e.g. writing) reliable rewards are hard, so R1 falls back to SFT + only a few hundred RL steps. (8) Unsuccessful attempts documented: PRM (hard to define fine-grained steps, hard to judge step correctness, reward hacking) and MCTS (token search space explosion, value-model training hard) both failed to scale. (9) Safety: jailbreakable; inherent safety only 'moderate' (~GPT-4o-2024-05-13) without an external risk-control system; refuses some queries after safety RL (hurts C-SimpleQA).
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: env-reward / verifiable-reward (effectively oracle-label for the training signal). The method fundamentally depends on a RELIABLE VERIFIER: ground-truth answers for math (rule/string match) and a compiler + test cases for code. The authors state the key to unlocking reasoning is 'hard reasoning questions, a reliable verifier and sufficient compute.' This is the discriminating variable: R1's self-reflection is incentivized via objective external/automated verification during training, not via intrinsic-only self-verification. At inference it self-verifies intrinsically (no external tool), but that ability was bought with verifiable-reward RL. Where no reliable verifier exists (writing, open-ended), the approach degrades to SFT/limited RL.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive but requires-(verifiable)-reward. With a reliable verifier, RL reliably and dramatically improves reasoning and the emergent self-verification/reflection genuinely raises accuracy on held-out reasoning benchmarks (distinct from the Huang-2023/'cannot self-correct yet' intrinsic-only negative result -- here the corrective skill is RL-trained against an oracle, not free intrinsic self-correction). Efficacy is contingent on a trustworthy reward signal; for tasks lacking one (writing), pure-RL self-improvement does not scale. So: strongly net-positive on verifiable reasoning, task-dependent / requires-oracle otherwise.
calibration_effect: mixed / largely not-measured as formal confidence calibration. The model exhibits productive 'reasoning tax' trade-offs: a language-consistency reward slightly degrades accuracy but improves readability; safety RL causes some over-refusal (lower C-SimpleQA). Overthinking on easy questions is documented (a soft over-allocation/overconfidence-in-need-to-reason effect). The paper does not report explicit ECE/Brier-style calibration metrics for answer confidence, so formal calibration is not-measured; behaviourally the effect is mixed (gains on hard problems, occasional overthinking/over-refusal).
failure_attribution_capability: n/a. DeepSeek-R1 is a reasoning-model training method, not a failure-attribution/diagnosis system; it does not classify failure modes into a taxonomy, attribute a responsible agent, or perform counterfactual step localization. (It uses only outcome-level verifiable rewards and documents its own 'unsuccessful attempts' qualitatively, but performs no algorithmic failure attribution.)
failure_mode_addressed: Targets the data-bottleneck and human-bias-ceiling of reasoning training (dependence on human-annotated CoT that caps performance at human-like reasoning) by letting RL discover non-human reasoning strategies. The emergent behaviours directly mitigate MAST-style failure modes: superficial/absent self-reflection (-> emergent reflection & self-verification), underthinking / premature termination on hard problems (-> learns to allocate more thinking time and explore alternatives). Conversely it can INDUCE overthinking (excess reasoning on easy items) and is exposed to reward hacking when the verifier is unreliable. R1-Zero's own failure modes (language mixing, poor readability) motivate the multi-stage R1.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new failure-trace benchmark. Released: model weights for DeepSeek-R1-Zero, DeepSeek-R1, and six distilled dense models (1.5B/7B/8B/14B/32B/70B) under MIT license; sample data used in rejection sampling and RL prompts; inference scripts. (Zenodo DOIs 10.5281/zenodo.15753193 and 10.5281/zenodo.15753347.) These open-weights/open-data releases are themselves the major reusable resource that seeded a large open RL-reasoning ecosystem.
builds_on: GRPO (Shao et al., 2024, DeepSeekMath) as the RL algorithm; PPO (Schulman et al., 2017) as the predecessor it simplifies; DeepSeek-V3 / DeepSeek-V3-Base (DeepSeek-AI, 2024) as the base model; chain-of-thought prompting (Wei et al., 2022) and 'let's think step by step' (Kojima et al., 2022); self-consistency / majority voting (Wang et al., 2022); OpenAI o1 (2024) as the inference-time-scaling reasoning-model paradigm it open-replicates; the RL-from-verifiable-reward / RLHF lineage (Ouyang et al. 2022). Implicitly part of the STaR / RL'd self-improvement-of-reasoning lineage (Zelikman et al. 2022; expert iteration). Explicitly contrasts with process reward models (Uesato 2022; Lightman 2023) and MCTS (AlphaGo/AlphaZero, Silver 2017) which it tried and abandoned.
extended_by_or_inspired: Catalyzed the 2025 'RL with verifiable rewards' (RLVR) and open-reasoning wave: open replications/analyses of R1-Zero such as Open-R1 (Hugging Face), TinyZero, SimpleRL-Zoo / SimpleRL-Reason, Logic-RL, Open-Reasoner-Zero, DAPO and Dr.GRPO (GRPO bias fixes); s1 / s1.1 budget-forcing and LIMO ('less is more' for reasoning); analyses of whether RL elicits vs. teaches reasoning (e.g. 'Does RLVR incentivize reasoning beyond the base model?', 'Spurious rewards' studies); reasoning distillation work (e.g. Sky-T1, Bespoke-Stratos, OpenThoughts). Directly informed DeepSeek-R1-0528 and subsequent reasoning models (Qwen3, Kimi k1.5/k2, etc.). Widely treated as the reference open reasoning model for studying emergent self-reflection.
citation_count: ~5,381 (Semantic Scholar, Nature version, paperId 2eed1fad9bbf887d4395de40f20144c4fafefd7f / CorpusID:275789950, as of June 2026). The arXiv preprint 2501.12948 is among the most-cited AI papers of 2025; combined preprint+journal citations are substantially higher (well into the thousands and rapidly growing).
reasoning_model_native: yes -- this IS a reasoning model and a defining instance of the o1/R1 era. DeepSeek-R1/-R1-Zero have built-in, always-on, RL-induced long-CoT reasoning with native (RL-emergent) self-reflection, verification and dynamic strategy adaptation; it is the open-weights archetype of a reasoning-model-native system with intrinsic reflection.
on_policy_distillation_link: strong / foundational on two axes. (1) RL itself is on-policy improvement: GRPO samples on-policy groups and updates the policy toward higher-reward (verified) trajectories -- self-distillation toward its own best reasoning. (2) Explicit knowledge distillation: ~800k on-policy DeepSeek-R1 trajectories are used to SFT smaller models, and the paper empirically shows distilling the large model's reasoning beats running RL on the small model. This positions R1 as a key reference for the on-policy-distillation / RLVR vs. distillation debate (teacher-trajectory SFT vs. small-model RL).
sample_efficiency: RL: gains accrue over thousands of RL steps (AIME 15.6%->71% across the training trajectory shown in Fig.1/2), with 16 rollouts/question and batch 512; substantial but not enormous step count by RL standards (reference model refreshed every 400 steps). Cold-start needs only 'thousands' of long-CoT examples; rejection-sampling SFT uses ~800k samples (600k reasoning + 200k non-reasoning, 2 epochs). The headline efficiency claim is data efficiency vs human annotation: no human-annotated reasoning traces are required for the core capability (only a verifier + hard questions). Distillation is highly sample/compute efficient at deployment (capability transferred to 1.5B-70B via SFT).
